title: Moin Moin in Cups
author: Iquo Bassey
desc: The shortcut version — a stew cooked separately and folded into the beans, steamed in cups under foil, with no beating at all.
longDesc: This is moin moin built the opposite way round. Instead of blending raw peppers into the batter and beating air into it, you cook a proper little stew first — oil, onion, tomato and pepper, fish and seasoning, fried until the tomato's sourness has gone — and fold that into the ground beans. There is no aeration step whatsoever, which makes it denser than the beaten version but far quicker and more forgiving. Steamed in cups under kitchen foil, it is done in forty to forty-five minutes.
ingredients: 1 cup brown or black-eyed beans, washed and peeled
2 cooking spoons tomato and pepper blend
// Used in the method but not listed in the original
steps: Wash the beans to remove the skin. Blend until smooth with very little water. The easiest route is to wash the beans the night before, soak them in water and leave them in the fridge — it goes much easier on your blender.
Heat the oil and fry the onion and the tomato and pepper blend. Add the fish and the seasoning. Taste for salt and correct the seasoning. Cook the stew until the tomato sourness goes off.
Pour the stew into the ground beans, add the ginger and mix well.
Add a little water to the beans if it is too thick. The consistency should not be too runny either.
Scoop the bean mixture into cups and place them in a big pot. Cover the cups with kitchen foil.
Add water at the base of the pot to help steam the beans. Add a little water at a time so the water does not cover the beans.
Moin moin will cook in 40 to 45 minutes.
chefTips: Cooking the stew first is the whole difference. It drives off the tomato's sourness before it ever reaches the beans, which the beaten version relies on the long steam to do.
An overnight cold soak in the fridge is her peeling method, and it is gentler on a domestic blender than pulsing.
There is no beating step. Accept that this will be denser than NGA022 — it is a different texture, not a failure.
Foil over each cup, not over the pot. It stops condensation dripping in and watering the top.
Water at the base only, added a little at a time. The cups must never be submerged.
Blend with very little water. The stew brings moisture of its own.
Ginger is unusual in moin moin and gives it a noticeably warmer finish. A teaspoon of paste is enough.
commonMistakes: Folding in a raw tomato blend instead of a cooked stew.
Letting the water rise over the cups.
Blending the beans with too much water before the stew goes in.
Expecting the light, risen texture of the beaten version.
sources: Adapted from 'How to make Moin Moin ( in cups)', byline '1Qfoodplatter'. Quantities as printed: 1 cup Brown black eye Beans (washed and peeled), 1/2 cup flaked steamed Mackerel Fish, 2 cooking spoons Tomato/Pepper blend, 1 teaspoon Ginger paste, 1-2 cooking spoons vegetable oil, crayfish seasoning to taste, salt to taste, cups for steaming.

The method is close to verbatim, including 'A good tip is to wash your beans the night before, soak in water and leave in the fridge and it will be easy on your blender'; 'Cook the stew until tomato sourness goes off'; 'Add a little water at a time so the water does not cover the beans'; and 'Moin moin will cook in 40–45 mins'.
LIST/METHOD MISMATCH, flagged: the method fries 'the onion' in step 2 but onion is not in the ingredient list. Listed above under a clear heading rather than inserted silently.
NOTE: the recipe is titled 'in cups' but gives no cup count and no yield. The serving figure here is a serving suggestion, not a sourced number.

TECHNIQUE DISAGREEMENT with NGA022, not reconciled: a stew is pre-cooked and folded in here, where Sisi Jemimah blends the raw peppers into the beans. And this page gives NO aeration step at all, against her 8 minutes plus 5 minutes of mixing. The steam times agree closely — 40 to 45 minutes here, 40 to 50 there.

DISAGREEMENT on the bean soak: overnight refrigerated here, against 10 minutes (Sisi Jemimah), 5 minutes lukewarm (her akara, NGA028) and 3 to 5 minutes (Ajoke, NGA005). This is the longest soak of the four and the only cold one.
healthBenefits: Cowpeas supply plant protein, folate and soluble fibre.
Mackerel contributes omega-3 fats and vitamin D.
culturalNote: Steaming moin moin in cups rather than leaves is the ordinary urban compromise, and it changes the dish in a way everybody notices and nobody can quite fix: the leaf contributes flavour as well as a vessel. The trade is convenience and a neat shape against that faint grassy perfume, and most Nigerian kitchens make it both ways depending on the occasion.
